Jimmy Blacklock

Republican candidate for Supreme Court, Chief Justice, Texas

Chief Justice, Supreme Court of Texas

Jimmy Blacklock is the incumbent Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Texas. Gov. Greg Abbott appointed him chief justice in January 2025, after he had served as a justice on the court since 2018. He was unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and faces Democrat Maggie Ellis in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Blacklock stands

Judicial philosophy / constitutional interpretation
Supports originalism. He argues that judges should not change the Constitution's meaning over time and that the people should change it through amendment.
Judicial pay and accountability
In his 2025 State of the Judiciary address, he called for raises for judges. He said he would use metrics such as clearance rates to identify 'problem judges' and push for their removal if necessary.
Bail
Supported the 2025 legislative effort to tighten restrictions on when defendants can be released on bail.
Child welfare
Called for changes to the child welfare system that would make it easier for families to stay together.
Political neutrality of the State Bar
In his 2025 State of the Judiciary address, he said the State Bar of Texas should 'remain completely politically neutral.'

Background

  • Chief Justice, Supreme Court of Texas, January 2025–present (appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott)
  • Justice, Supreme Court of Texas, 2018–2025 (appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott)
  • General counsel to Gov. Greg Abbott, 2015–2018
  • Texas Attorney General's Office under Greg Abbott, 2009–2015
  • Law clerk to Judge Jerry Smith, U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit
  • J.D., Yale Law School
